problem: The text says the leftmost bit of a 7-bit word is c₇, but a 7-bit word has coefficients c₀ to c₆. This also contradicts the formula given two lines later (c_{n−1} is the leftmost, i.e. c₆) and the worked example, where the message 1101 is called x³ + x² + 1 with the leftmost bit as the x³ coefficient.
fix: Number the bits from the right. The rightmost bit is c₀ (constant term); the leftmost is c₆ in a 7-bit word (in general c_{n−1}).

problem: "Keeps the message in the first k positions" is ambiguous, because the chapter has just numbered positions from the right (c₀, c₁, …). A student can read "first k" as c₀…c_{k−1}, which is exactly the parity-on-the-left mistake listed in the exam traps.
fix: Say: systematic form keeps the k message bits in the highest-order positions (the x^{n−1} down to x^{n−k} coefficients, sent first) and appends the n − k parity bits at the right end, in positions x^{n−k−1} down to x⁰.
